The Addlink S90 Lite comes in the 512GB, 1TB, 2TB, and 4TB capacities, although the 4TB model seems difficult to find. At the time of review these are on sale for $38.88, $59.88, and $109.99, respectively. This is competitive with similar drives like the Silicon Power UD90, the Team Group MP44L, and the WD Black SN770, to name a few. Some drives in this class have moved to QLC at 2TB while our S90 Lite sample has TLC, which makes this drive most attractive at that capacity.

The S90 Lite is capable of up to 5,000/4,200 MBps for sequential reads and writes, and 780K/800K IOPS for random reads and writes. There is no official TBW but Addlink indicates the warranty is based on “percentage used” by SMART. The warranty is good for five years.

The Addlink S90 Lite is a solid-state drive in the M.2 2280 form factor, launched on June 22nd, 2022. It is available in capacities ranging from 512 GB to 4 TB. This page reports specifications for the 512 GB variant. With the rest of the system, the Addlink S90 Lite interfaces using a PCI-Express 4.0 x4 connection. The SSD controller is the PS5021-E21T from Phison, a DRAM cache is not available. Addlink has installed 176-layer TLC NAND flash on the S90 Lite, the flash chips are made by Micron. To improve write speeds, a pseudo-SLC cache is used, so bursts of incoming writes are soaked up more quickly. Thanks to support for the fast PCI-Express 4.0 interface, performance is excellent. The S90 Lite is rated for sequential read speeds of up to 5,000 MB/s and 2,500 MB/s write; random IOPS reach up to 250K for reads and 350K for writes. At its launch, the SSD was priced at 39 USD. The warranty length is set to five years, which is an excellent warranty period. The TBW rating for the Addlink S90 Lite 512 GB is unknown.
